column5: lead and guide for your name's sake
column6: The commentary asks God to guide the worshipers along the way; this psalm asks God, as refuge, to lead and guide the speaker for his name's sake.

column5: instruction and counsel on the way
column6: The commentary presents guidance as ongoing accompaniment; God promises here to instruct and teach the way, keeping watch and giving counsel.

column5: light and truth lead to the holy hill
column6: The commentary's route ends in God's welcoming presence; the psalm asks God to send light and truth to lead the speaker to the holy mountain and dwelling.

column5: our guide forever
column6: The commentary's “us” asks God for guidance as a community; this psalm says of God, “this is our God,” who guides us forever.

column5: make me walk the path of your commands
column6: The commentary asks for a route that is actually walked; this prayer asks God to make the speaker walk the path of the commandments and says that he delights in it.

column5: a lamp to the feet and light to the path
column6: The commentary develops guidance through signs and landmarks; the psalm calls God's word a lamp for the feet and a light on the path.

column5: make my steps firm; do not let sin rule
column6: The commentary asks for continuing guidance and protection from leaving the way; this prayer asks God to make the speaker's steps firm and keep wrongdoing from ruling him.

column5: feet set on rock; steps made firm
column6: The commentary's traveler needs support to move steadily after losing the way; the psalm describes being lifted from a pit, set on rock, and given firm steps.

column5: God led Israel like a flock
column6: The commentary develops the guide who goes ahead of dependent travelers; this poetic retelling says God led Israel safely like a flock through the wilderness.

column5: God guards the paths of justice
column6: The commentary joins the straight path to just balance and right conduct; Proverbs says God guards the paths of justice and preserves the way of his faithful ones.

column5: the righteous path brightens as daybreak
column6: The commentary stresses that guidance is a continuing walk, not a single arrival; Proverbs pictures the righteous path growing brighter until full day.

column5: God directs the steps
column6: The commentary says even worshipers already on the way need God to lead them at each step; Proverbs distinguishes a person's plans from the Lord's direction of the steps.

column5: road markers for the returning traveler
column6: The commentary develops signs and landmarks that help a traveler find the route; Jeremiah tells the returning people to set up road markers and guideposts and remember the highway they traveled.

column5: God chooses a protective detour
column6: The commentary's “straight path” is a divinely chosen route, not merely the shortest line; God deliberately does not lead Israel by the Philistine road because seeing war might make them return to Egypt.

column5: the detour protects Israel from turning back
column6: The commentary treats guidance as God's care for travelers; the Mekhilta reads the longer Exodus route as protective pedagogy, since the newly freed people might turn back when faced with war.

column5: a messenger goes ahead and brings Israel to the prepared place
column6: The commentary's guide leads from the front and brings travelers to their destination; God promises to send a messenger ahead of Israel to guard them and bring them to the prepared place.

column5: prepare a straight highway for God
column6: The commentary hears a path that must be made straight and walked; Isaiah calls for a straight highway in the wilderness as the Lord comes to his people.

column5: the shepherd gathers lambs and gently leads
column6: The commentary describes both a guide who goes ahead and a dependent traveler who needs support; Isaiah pictures God carrying lambs close and gently leading the nursing sheep.

column5: God teaches Ephraim to walk and takes him by the arms
column6: The commentary portrays a traveler who sways and needs support; God recalls teaching Ephraim to walk and taking him by the arms, though Ephraim did not recognize the healing.

column5: leading with cords of kindness
column6: The commentary connects guidance with gentle, loving care rather than payment; Hosea describes God leading Israel with human kindness and cords of love.

column5: God shepherds and gives the flock rest
column6: The commentary asks for a guide who leads dependent travelers to a place of welcome; God promises to shepherd his own flock and make them lie down in safety.

column5: wilderness turned into pools and dry ground into springs
column6: The commentary connects the route with sustaining water and the land's life-giving support; this verse pictures God transforming the wilderness into pools and dry ground into springs.

column5: a blind guide and a blind follower both fall
column6: The commentary says a guide who cannot see the route cannot lead others; Jesus asks whether a blind person can guide another blind person without both falling into a pit.

column5: the Father draws people to the Son
column6: The commentary insists that ultimate guidance belongs to God; Jesus says no one can come to him unless the Father draws that person.

column5: walk in the light before darkness overtakes you
column6: The commentary warns that the traveler can lose the way after having found it; Jesus tells his hearers to walk while they have the light, lest darkness overtake them and leave them unable to know where they are going.

column5: God makes a way out of temptation
column6: The commentary pictures an ambush on the straight path and asks for continued guidance; Paul says God will not let testing exceed what can be borne and will provide a way of escape.

column5: a generation that strays in heart and does not know God's ways
column6: The commentary says guidance must be renewed because people can turn aside after being led; Hebrews recalls the wilderness generation as continually straying in heart and not knowing God's ways.

column5: those led by God's Spirit are God's children
column6: The commentary makes divine guidance the continuing mark of those who worship God; Paul identifies those led by God's Spirit as children of God.

column5: two ways, light and darkness, under opposed powers
column6: The commentary sets the straight path against straying and describes an adversary lying in wait on it; Barnabas develops two moral ways, light and darkness, under God's angels and Satan's angels.
